EXPORTS REACHABILITY PROBED AT RUNTIME (method designed by pij-related-koala, run by the o-prime in this repo; script committed as scripts/exports-reachability-probe.mjs). An exports map does not merely FAIL TO LIST a subpath, it FORBIDS it — reachability is a runtime fact (ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED), not a barrel-file reading, so the module exports it and a consumer can import it are different questions. Probe run against a scratch project with node_modules/@ai-substrate/dd symlinked to this repo, on node v24.7.0, WITH POSITIVE CONTROLS (a zero result proves nothing if the probe is broken): control 1 root export reachable PASS, control 2 undeclared path forbidden PASS, control 3 declared-path-wrong-extension forbidden PASS. RESULT: 11 of 12 consumed subpaths reachable; ./plan is FORBIDDEN with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. This confirms koala paper check as a runtime fact and sharpens OQ-2 materially: the question is not merely whether plan SHOULD be public but that under todays map harness CANNOT CONSUME IT AT ALL — a hard error at import, not a workaround, affecting 9 symbols across acts/plan/index.ts and acts/plan/pr-body.ts. SECOND FINDING, a real defect the probe surfaced incidentally: the root export . resolves to dist/index.js which IS THE BIN ENTRY (src/index.ts carries the node shebang and calls main()), so import @ai-substrate/dd EXECUTES THE CLI as an import side effect, printing help to stdout, and yields ZERO named exports. koala predicted this from the same defect in harness-engineering own package. Not blocking harness (it imports subpaths, never the root) but freezing the map would freeze the defect.
